prayerExcerpt.en-US: The flock of the faithful may always find shepherds after your own heart.

cards.excerptSource: content/of/formularies/sanctoral/06-06.json collect (petition clause; en-US capitalised and cut before 'and be fed', pt-BR verbatim)
cards.subject: Half-length, bareheaded, in the all-white habit of the Premonstratensian canons: a white cassock, a white linen rochet and a short white shoulder cape, the white pallium with small black crosses of an archbishop. He holds up a gold sunburst monstrance in his right hand and a tall archiepiscopal cross with two crossbars in his left, and a small olive branch rests against the cross. Background: the wooded valley of Prémontré in the forest of Coucy, northern France, with the first small abbey church of pale stone among the trees and a stream in the meadow below.
cards.face: A man of about forty-five, clean-shaven, with a long, smooth, egg-shaped face narrowing evenly to a rounded chin — a long, fine, straight nose, dark almond-shaped eyes under thin, high-arched brows, smooth cheeks with little modelling, a small, firm mouth with a full lower lip; short dark-brown hair cut round the head with a broad clerical tonsure on the crown, and a calm, noble, slightly reserved look.
cards.basis: Follows the Flemish Baroque tradition, as in Gaspar de Crayer's 1664 Norbert: a clean-shaven, oval-faced canon with short dark hair in the white habit, with the monstrance and the double-barred cross of the archbishop of Magdeburg. He was archbishop from his mid-forties and died at about fifty-four.

cards.subject: Half-length, a Syrian monk-deacon: a plain black monastic habit with the black hood drawn up over the head, and a narrow white deacon's stole (orarion) over the left shoulder. He holds a reed pen in his right hand over an open codex resting on a small wooden lectern, the pages covered only with faint lines, no legible writing; beside him a small wooden lyre recalls his title, the Harp of the Spirit. Background: Edessa (Urfa) under a warm evening sky, the citadel on its rocky hill with two tall columns, and the fish pools of Abraham among cypresses below.
cards.face: A small, slight Syrian man of about sixty with an olive-brown complexion and a short, compact face — a broad, low forehead with fine lines, a short, blunt nose with a small hook, large, dark, luminous, deep-set eyes under thin arching brows, flat, lean cheeks, a small, soft chin and a wide, thin-lipped mouth; only a few wisps of grey hair at the temples under the hood, a sparse grey moustache and a thin wisp of beard at the chin (beardless by nature), and a rapt, singing look lifted toward the light.
cards.basis: Dionysius's Painter's Manual describes him as an old man with sparse hair and little beard, wearing a mantle; the Syriac icons show him in a black monk's hood writing his hymns. The olive complexion follows his birth at Nisibis.

sources.title: Dionysius of Fourna, Manuel d'iconographie chrétienne (Didron, 1845)

name.en-US: Sts. John Fisher and Thomas More
name.pt-BR: Santos João Fisher e Tomás More

prayerExcerpt.en-US: Nothing can come but that that God will.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Nada pode acontecer senão aquilo que Deus quer.

cards.excerptSource: Thomas More, letter to Margaret Roper from the Tower, 1534 (Rogers no. 206), in the modern-spelling text of the Center for Thomas More Studies, https://thomasmorestudies.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Letters-205-206-D-on-Conscience-10-9-2025.pdf; pt-BR our rendering. The feast has no proper formulary in the repo.
cards.subject: Two half-length figures side by side, as on the Philip and James card. Left, Bishop John Fisher of Rochester in a black skullcap-like bishop's cap with side flaps, a white linen rochet over a purple cassock and a black chimere, holding a plain wooden crucifix against his breast and a martyr's palm; a cardinal's red hat lies at the lower edge beside him. Right, Sir Thomas More as Holbein painted him: a soft black cap, a black gown with a broad brown fur collar over deep red velvet sleeves, the gold collar of SS links with the Tudor rose pendant across his shoulders, a small closed prayer book in his hands. Background: the Thames under a pale grey-blue sky with the White Tower of the Tower of London and its walls on the far bank. Keep both figures inside the arched window.
cards.face: Fisher: a tall, lean man of about sixty-five, clean-shaven, with a long, gaunt, bony face — a high, broad forehead, prominent cheekbones above hollowed cheeks, a long, straight, prominent nose, large, wide-open pale grey eyes under high, thin brows, lines running down from the nose past the mouth, a long, firm chin and a thin, straight, closed mouth; grey hair hidden under the cap, and a steady, searching gaze. More: a man of about fifty-five, clean-shaven with the faintest shadow of stubble, with a straight-sided, rather square face — a broad forehead, a long, straight nose with a slightly rounded tip, grey-blue eyes under straight dark brows with a small vertical crease between them, firm, slightly sunken cheeks, a square chin and a straight, composed mouth with a hint of wry humour; straight dark auburn-brown hair falling to the ears under the black cap, the face in three-quarter view looking off to the side. Fisher is older, paler and much thinner; More is fuller in the face, darker-haired and fair-skinned with a light flush.
cards.basis: Both faces follow Hans Holbein the Younger, who drew and painted them from life: Fisher's chalk drawing of about 1527 (a long, gaunt, clean-shaven face with wide eyes) and More's 1527 portrait in the Frick Collection. Erasmus's 1519 letter to Hutten confirms More's fair complexion, auburn-black hair and blue-grey eyes.

sources.title: Wikimedia Commons, Hans Holbein the Younger, John Fisher (drawing, c. 1527)
Wikimedia Commons, Hans Holbein the Younger, Sir Thomas More (1527, Frick Collection)
Erasmus, letter to Ulrich von Hutten, 23 July 1519 (Center for Thomas More Studies)
Wikipedia, John Fisher

cards.subject: Half-length Greek patriarch in the Byzantine manner: a close-fitting white cap covering the head, marked with black crosses (his mark in Byzantine art), a white phelonion patterned with black crosses, a white omophorion with large black crosses over the shoulders. His right hand is raised in blessing; his left holds a small icon of the Mother of God with the Child (Theotokos) against his breast. Background: the harbour of Alexandria under a clear sky, the tall Pharos lighthouse on its island, white city walls and palms along the shore.
cards.face: An Alexandrian Greek of about sixty with a warm olive complexion and a long, oblong face with a strong frame — a straight, high-bridged nose with a narrow ridge, intense dark eyes under strong, dark, slightly knitted brows angled down toward the nose, high cheekbones, a firm, set mouth; the hair hidden by the cap except a little greying brown at the temples, and a long, full brown beard streaked with grey, tapering to a single point on the chest; a fierce, resolute, watchful look.
cards.basis: Follows the 14th-century fresco in the Chora church, Istanbul (the white cap with crosses, a long tapering brown beard, knitted brows), which agrees with Dionysius's grey-haired, long-bearded Cyril in a cross-marked head-covering, and Tzanes's 1654 icon. The icon of the Theotokos recalls the Council of Ephesus.

sources.title: Wikimedia Commons, Cyril of Alexandria, fresco in the Chora church

cards.subject: Half-length widowed queen as on her own tomb effigy in Coimbra: the grey-brown habit of a Franciscan tertiary with a knotted cord, a close white wimple and a black veil, and a slender gold crown set on the veil. In the gathered fold of her habit she holds a few red and white roses; her other hand holds a pilgrim's staff with a small scallop shell (from her pilgrimage to Compostela). No children. Background: Coimbra on the river Mondego, the Gothic monastery church of Santa Clara on the near bank and the white city climbing the hill opposite.
cards.face: A woman of about fifty-five with a fair Iberian complexion and a long, rectangular face with a high forehead and a long, straight jaw — a slender, slightly aquiline nose, wide-set, heavy-lidded grey-green eyes under fine, arched brown brows, high, flat cheekbones with a soft flush, a small, full-lipped mouth with a faint, gentle smile; the hair hidden by the wimple, and a serene, kindly gaze toward the roses.
cards.basis: No portrait from life survives; the dress follows her tomb effigy (1330, Santa Clara-a-Nova, Coimbra), carved to her instructions, showing her crowned in a Poor Clare habit with a pilgrim's staff and purse, and the roses follow her usual iconography. The face is our choice for a mature queen, made older than the young Elizabeth of Hungary card.

sources.title: Wikimedia Commons, tomb of Queen Saint Isabel, Santa Clara-a-Nova, Coimbra
Wikipedia, Elizabeth of Portugal

cards.subject: Half-length, a very tall, big-framed priest in the black cassock and mantle of the Camillians, with the large red cloth cross sewn on the breast. He bends slightly toward a sick old man propped on white pillows in a hospital bed at the lower corner, one arm around his shoulders and the other hand holding a small crucifix for him to see; the patient is decently covered with a white sheet. Background: the long vaulted ward of the hospital of Santo Spirito in Sassia, Rome, with rows of curtained beds and high arched windows, the dome of St Peter's seen through one window.
cards.face: A man of about fifty-five with a long, rectangular face and a heavy, square jaw — a large, long nose, broad at the bridge, deep-set, slightly hooded grey-brown eyes under thick, straight dark brows, lines running from the nose to the corners of a wide, firm mouth, lean cheeks; close-cropped dark hair greying and receding from a high forehead, a short, clipped dark beard and moustache flecked with grey, and a compassionate, weathered look down at the sick man.
cards.basis: The painted portraits and early engravings agree on close-cropped receding hair, a short beard or stubble and a long, strong face with a large nose; his biographers record his great height. He founded the Ministers of the Sick in his thirties and died at sixty-four.

cards.subject: Half-length Capuchin friar in the rough brown habit with the long pointed hood lying on the shoulders and a white knotted cord. He holds a crucifix raised high in his right hand, as when he rode before the imperial army in 1601, and a closed book (his sermons and Hebrew scholarship) against his side with the left. Background: the open Hungarian plain near Székesfehérvár under a wide sky, the small walled town with its church towers in the distance and far-off white tents and banners of the camp; no fighting.
cards.face: A man of about forty-two with a broad-browed, strong face — a wide, high forehead, prominent, rounded cheekbones, a straight nose with a thick, rounded tip, large, dark, eager eyes under thick black brows, a wide mouth; short dark hair around a Capuchin tonsure, a very long, thick, dark-brown beard falling to the chest, and a fervent, commanding gaze lifted toward the crucifix.
cards.basis: His portraits show a Capuchin with a very long beard, bald in old age; the card shows him at forty-two, the age he was at the battle of Székesfehérvár (1601), so the beard is still dark. The raised crucifix is from the accounts of that battle.

cards.subject: Half-length fifth-century bishop, bareheaded, in a full, bell-shaped deep gold chasuble over a white alb and the white pallium with small dark crosses, as in the Ravenna mosaics. He holds an open book of his sermons in the left hand and raises the right, open, in the gesture of a preacher. Background: Ravenna under a soft sky, the round brick bell tower and long basilica of Sant'Apollinare in Classe among umbrella pines, with the flat marsh toward the sea.
cards.face: A man of about sixty with a broad, rounded, full face — a wide, smooth forehead with a receding hairline, a short, straight nose with a rounded tip, kind dark eyes set wide apart and creased at the corners, full, rounded cheeks, a broad, full-lipped mouth slightly open as if speaking, a soft, round chin; thin, short grey hair and a short, round-trimmed grey beard, and a warm, eloquent look.
cards.basis: His contemporary mosaic portrait in San Giovanni Evangelista, Ravenna, is lost; the later engraved portraits show a balding bishop with a short beard, which the card follows. The golden chasuble alludes to his name, 'golden-worded'.

cards.subject: Half-length, kneeling in adoration, hands joined at the breast: a black cassock with the white-edged French clerical bands (rabat) at the throat, as in his portraits. Before him, on a white-clothed altar to one side, a gold sunburst monstrance with the Host exposed between tall candles. Background: the chapel of his first house of perpetual adoration in Paris, simple white walls and a round window, with the grey rooftops of Paris outside.
cards.face: A slight man of about fifty-five, clean-shaven, with a long, narrow face tapering to a pointed chin — a very high, domed forehead with the hair receding at the temples, a long, straight nose with a fine ridge, deep-set, intense grey-blue eyes under thin, straight brows, hollow cheeks under distinct cheekbones, a thin, compressed mouth; brown hair greying and combed back, falling behind the ears to the collar, and a rapt gaze fixed on the Host.
cards.basis: Follows his 19th-century photographs and the La Seyne portrait: a thin, clean-shaven face with a very high, receding forehead, deep-set eyes and hair worn long behind the ears, in cassock and French bands. He died at fifty-seven.

cards.excerptSource: content/of/formularies/sanctoral/08-07.json collect (petition clause, verbatim in both languages, capitalised)
cards.subject: Two half-length figures side by side, as on the Philip and James card. Left and slightly larger, Pope Sixtus II, bareheaded, in a gold brocade cope lined with red over a white alb, holding a martyr's palm, seated in the stone bishop's chair of the catacomb as when he was seized while teaching. Right, a little behind, his deacon Agapitus in a red dalmatic, holding a closed gospel book with a jewelled cover. Background: a catacomb chamber on the Appian Way, a low vaulted room of warm tufa with plain marble slabs set in the walls (no lettering) and small clay oil lamps giving a golden light, a shaft of daylight from a light-well above. Keep both figures inside the arched window.
cards.face: Sixtus: a man of about sixty-five with a LONG, LEAN, NARROW face — a high, completely bald dome with only thin wisps of white at the temples, a long, strongly hooked nose, heavy-lidded pale blue eyes under thin white brows, flat cheeks, a long upper lip and a thin mouth; CLEAN-SHAVEN but for close white stubble on the jaw (no beard, no curls), the head slightly bowed and the gaze lowered gently toward the viewer as he teaches. Agapitus: a man of about thirty with a wide, flat-planed, rectangular face and a broad, square chin with a small cleft — a short, straight nose, wide-set level dark eyes under heavy straight black brows, a full mouth; close-cropped straight black hair, clean-shaven with a dark shadow on the jaw, looking toward the pope.
cards.basis: No early portrait of Sixtus survives; the card follows Raphael's Sistine Madonna (a bald, hook-nosed pope with a short curly grey beard looking upward); the card keeps his bald dome and hooked nose but drops the beard and the upward gaze, which would repeat the Cornelius card. Agapitus is one of the deacons martyred with him in the Liber Pontificalis; his face is our choice, kept apart from the Lawrence card.

sources.title: Wikimedia Commons, Raphael, Saint Sixtus (detail of the Sistine Madonna)
Wikipedia, Pope Sixtus II
